T1.notes: Built by script t1.py with expect_dv on every feature; STL volume 0.05 % above the SolidWorks volume (facet size); STL bounds [0,0,0]-[80,50,46] (model frame, one shell); STEP is in mm.

T2.notes: Opened bracket.SLDPRT, Save-As bracket_b first, then added features. Hand volume = T1 hand volume minus 4 counterbore rings (pi(5^2-2.75^2)*3 each) minus slot ((14*6+pi*9)*6).

T3.notes: Peak is on the compressive side of the R4 fillet (load +X bends the upright toward +X, so x=0 is the tension face). The 2-element exclusion hid fixed-hole-wall edge nodes at 24.4 MPa (el 2.0) that rise with the mesh (22.8, 24.4, 26.8, 33.4 at el 3, 2, 1.5, 1.0): a fixture singularity. A fixed 4 mm exclusion gives 15.05, 15.52, 15.58 for el 3, 2, 1.5. Layer stress (sigma_zz) 10.14, 10.19, 10.22. Pure-cantilever hand deflection of the upright is 0.31 mm; FEA 2.36 mm, the rest is flexure of the 6 mm base between the screws, estimated by hand at about 1.5 to 2 mm, not checked more closely.

T4.how_judged: The inside-corner peak rises with every refinement (14.5, 16.4, 17.4, 20.7 MPa, steps of +13, +6, +19 %) so it is a singularity, not a stress, and no value is reported for it; judged instead by the converged tension across layers (11.46, 11.54, 11.55, 11.53 MPa, sigma_zz on the back face near the root), which gives SF_layer 1.95 below 2.0, and by the corner-line averages that hold steady (1 mm: 9.9 then 9.7 MPa; 2 mm: 6.9 then 7.0 MPa).
T4.notes: The yield criterion cannot be certified for the sharp corner (the peak never converges); the layer criterion fails on a converged number. Node counts of the averages were not recorded. The el 1.0 run had 378,649 nodes, above the 150,000 asked for.

T5.print_orientation: base on the bed, layers stacked along Z (unchanged)
T5.notes: No design change was needed because the T3 bracket meets the requirement on the converged study, so T5's condition was not met. bracket_c.SLDPRT is an unchanged file copy of bracket.SLDPRT, saved so the file exists, not a new design. From the same T3 stress field, tension across layers would be 14.9 MPa (SF 1.51, fails) with layers stacked along X and 5.5 MPa (SF 4.1) along Y, i.e. printing on the y=0 side face would raise the margin; not adopted or checked for printability.

T6.solver: Intel direct sparse (direct sparse requested through the macro; it reads back as 7)
T6.how_pin_was_stabilised: Two soft pad rings (E 0.5 MPa, nu 0.45, r 5.0 to 6.5, 2 mm thick, y 15.2 to 17.2, a 0.2 mm gap off the block face) bonded to the pin ends, their outer faces fixed; the pin is split into three bodies (middle plus two ends) so the end loads go on the protruding cylinder faces.
T6.why: Reaction 500.001 N against 500 N applied; the pin axis rises 0.1285 mm = the 0.1 mm radial gap plus 0.028 mm block rise, penetration 0.0001 mm; without the contact set the pin rises 8.77 mm and the solver reports excessive displacement; pads carry at most about 4.5 N (pad vm 0.062 MPa), under 1 %; peak 4.678 then 4.663 MPa (0.3 %) at 86,188 then 149,353 nodes; hole-top compressive sigma_zz 6.1 to 6.5 MPa against Hertz 6.8; pin bending stress 31.0 MPa against 31.8 by hand.
T6.notes: Hand: projected bearing F/(d L) = 500/(10*30) = 1.667 MPa; Hertz line contact for the clearance fit (R* 255 mm, E* 2199 MPa, a 1.57 mm) gives p_max 6.8 MPa. First attempt with pad rings bonded to the block face gave an 85 to 90 MPa spike at the hole mouth all round, including the unloaded bottom: an artefact, discarded. Frictionless contact; about 5 elements across the contact width.
